_comment: Worked verification examples ('how we verify'). Single source of truth rendered by index.html (entries with onHome=true, using traceShort) and validation.html (all entries, using traceFull). claim/trace values are trusted site-authored HTML — never put API or user text here. Badge label values: ok=Verified, pending=Pending, nuanced=Nuanced. sourceIds feeds cite-badge.js and each id must exist in data/sources.json.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: top five roots
caseStudies.claimHome: The five most frequent roots in the Qur'an: a-l-h (God, 2,851), q-w-l (say, 1,722), k-w-n (be, 1,390), r-b-b (Lord, 980), a-m-n (believe, 879).
caseStudies.claim: a-l-h (God, 2,851), q-w-l (say, 1,722), k-w-n (be, 1,390), r-b-b (Lord, 980), a-m-n (believe, 879).
caseStudies.traceShort: Traced to the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus (Dukes 2009–2017), corpus.quran.com dictionary. Full table on Numbers.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus, Kais Dukes 2009–2017, GPL-licensed. Dictionary interface at corpus.quran.com. Full top-10 with per-root citations on Numbers and Roots. One primary source; independent triangulation possible via any Qur'anic concordance.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: Farahi's Mufradat and Niẓām
caseStudies.claimHome: Farahi's Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an are foundational to the coherence-based reading school.
caseStudies.claim: Hamiduddin Farahi, Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an. Foundational to the coherence-based reading school.
caseStudies.traceShort: Corroborated by Mustansir Mir's 1986 monograph on Islahi's nazm method. Nuanced, not Verified: no modern edition or page of Farahi's own works has been checked here. Full citations on Sources.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Primary: Farahi's own Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an. Independent secondary corroboration: Mustansir Mir, Coherence in the Qur'an: A Study of Islahi's Concept of Nazm in Tadabbur-i Qur'an (Indianapolis: American Trust Publications, 1986, ISBN 9780892590650) — a scholarly monograph devoted to showing that Islahi's nazm method, and by extension the whole coherence-based reading school, descends directly from Farahi's Mufradat and Niẓām. The secondary source corroborates the lineage; the primary record does not yet name a verifiable modern edition or page, so this stays Nuanced rather than Verified. Full citations on Sources.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: y-w-m (day)
caseStudies.claimHome: Root y-w-m (day) occurs 405 times in the Leeds corpus. Widely circulated totals such as 365 or 475 count selected surface or compound forms instead; this site has not reproduced those totals.
caseStudies.claim: Root y-w-m occurs 405 times under the Leeds corpus's root annotation. Claims of 365 or 475 use different selections of surface and compound forms; they are not results reproduced by this site.
caseStudies.traceShort: Only the 405 root total is verified here. The other totals are retained as cautions about changing the unit of count, not endorsed as findings. See Numbers.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why it stays Nuanced. The 405 total is recomputed from the cited Leeds root annotations. The often-repeated 365 and 475 totals use other, usually unstated selection rules; no inspected source or reproducible procedure for them is presently in this site's evidence record. They are mentioned only to show why the unit and inclusion rule must be declared, not as verified alternatives. Detail on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: mercy travels with forgiveness
caseStudies.claimHome: Of every root it ever shares a verse with, r-ḥ-m (mercy) appears most often beside gh-f-r (forgiveness) — together in 91 verses, far ahead of any other pairing.
caseStudies.claim: The root r-ḥ-m (mercy) co-occurs with gh-f-r (forgiveness) in 91 verses — its most frequent verse-mate by a wide margin (its next-closest partner shares 37).
caseStudies.traceShort: Counted from the bundled co-occurrence tables (Leeds v0.4); the same pairing tops the list from gh-f-r's side too. Explore on Roots.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted from this site's bundled verse-level co-occurrence tables (data/cooccurrence/), derived from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 — recomputable from the data we ship. r-ḥ-m and gh-f-r share 91 verses; r-ḥ-m's next-closest partner shares 37, and the pairing is also the top result from gh-f-r's side (91), so it is not an artefact of one root's raw frequency. The count is descriptive: it shows the two ideas are voiced together, not what any verse means. Open either root on Roots to see its co-occurrence network.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: hapax legomena
caseStudies.claim: 12,004 surface forms (out of 18,993 unique forms) occur exactly once in the Qur'an. 395 roots (out of 1,642) occur exactly once.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed directly from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 word-form and root tables, which are bundled in this site's own data/morphology/ files — so the claim is recomputable by anyone, from the data this site ships, without trusting us. Published on Numbers at Study depth.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: a two-source claim
caseStudies.claim: 547 roots appear only in Meccan surahs; 198 appear only in Medinan surahs.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why two sources. This claim combines the Leeds corpus (which roots occur in which surahs) with the Cairo 1924 edition's Meccan/Medinan classification. The badge cites both; click it to see the pair. A nuance rides along: a handful of surahs are classified differently in other traditions, so the boundary counts can shift by a few under other schemes — the claim on Numbers carries that note beside it.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: "this world" and "the hereafter"
caseStudies.claim: A popular claim holds that "this world" (al-dunyā) and "the hereafter" (al-ākhira) each occur exactly 115 times. At the root level the counts are not equal: d-n-w occurs 133 times and a-kh-r 250 times. The 115/115 parity holds only for particular surface forms under one counting rule.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why it stays Nuanced. The often-repeated "115 each" figure counts specific surface forms (such as the definite al-dunyā and al-ākhira) under one selection rule. At the level this site computes — the triliteral root — the counts differ: d-n-w appears 133 times and a-kh-r 250 times (a-kh-r also carries senses like "last" and "other"), both verified from the Leeds corpus and recomputable from data/roots-summary.json. We report the honest root numbers and note that a matched count depends entirely on which forms one chooses to count — the same caution the y-w-m example makes. This site does not endorse numerical-parity claims it cannot reproduce.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: corpus size
caseStudies.claim: The bundled corpus holds 77,429 word-units across 6,236 verses, carrying 1,642 distinct triliteral roots.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted by scripts/build-numbers.mjs directly from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 morphology bundled in data/morphology/, so anyone can recount from the data this site ships. These three totals are the denominators behind every frequency and density figure on Numbers; the counting rule and its alternatives are documented on Coverage.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: root coverage
caseStudies.claim: 49,967 of 77,429 word-units (64.53%) carry a triliteral root; the rest are mostly particles, pronouns, and other function words that have no root by definition.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Measured by scripts/compute-coverage.mjs over every bundled morphology word-unit; the full field-by-field report, including the part-of-speech breakdown of the rootless remainder, is published on Coverage. Marked Nuanced because the share depends on the corpus's annotation choices: it bounds what any root-based statistic here can describe, which is why it is worth citing at all.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: believers' vocative, 89 verses
caseStudies.claim: The formula "ya ayyuha alladhina amanu" (O you who believe) opens 89 verses across the Qur'an.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus morphology by scripts/build-rhetorical-features.mjs, written to data/rhetorical-features.json. Full list on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: fawatih, 29 surahs / 14 combinations
caseStudies.claim: 29 surahs open with a sequence of isolated letters (fawatih), in 14 distinct combinations.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus by scripts/build-rhetorical-features.mjs, written to data/rhetorical-features.json. Full breakdown on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: point-pair symmetry, 0 of 3,067
caseStudies.claim: 3,067 candidate root pairs tested for mirrored position around a surah's centre; 0 reached significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-symmetry-test.mjs, written to data/symmetry-test.json. Method and closest near-misses on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: block-level symmetry, 0 of 345
caseStudies.claim: 345 candidates across four block-level mirror-symmetry tests, pooled corpus-wide; 0 reached significance after correction.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-structure-tests.mjs over the sections in data/structure/, written to data/structure-tests.json. Method and closest near-misses on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: surah 91, mean run length 15
caseStudies.claim: Surah 91 (al-Shams) is a monorhyme: all 15 verses share one rhyme-ending key, for a mean run length of 15, the maximum possible value.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus by scripts/build-rhyme-map.mjs, written to data/rhyme-summary.json and data/rhyme/91.json. Rhyme regularity ranking on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: r-h-m / gh-f-r association scores
caseStudies.claim: r-h-m (mercy) and gh-f-r (forgive) share 91 verses: PMI 3.17, Dice 0.353, LLR 302.86, gh-f-r's top partner by every measure.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-association-stats.mjs, written to data/association/ (per-root files). Method note in data/association/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: r-h-m network centrality
caseStudies.claim: r-h-m ranks 32nd of 1,642 roots by degree centrality, 56th by betweenness, and 53rd by eigenvector centrality, over the root co-occurrence graph.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-centrality.mjs, written to data/centrality/ (per-root files). Method note in data/centrality/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: discursive pivots, 137 occurrences
caseStudies.claim: 137 verses open with a temporal particle (idh, idha, or lamma) while sharing a content root with the verse before them.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-discursive-pivots.mjs, written to data/discursive-pivots.json. Full list on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: association-pairs export, 5,211 rows
caseStudies.claim: The downloadable association-pairs table has 5,211 rows: the deduplicated union of every root's top-25-by-LLR partner list.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Generated by scripts/build-exports.mjs, written to data/exports/association-pairs.csv and .json. Download and schema on Export.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: vocabulary variety by period (TTR, MATTR, MTLD)
caseStudies.claim: Raw form TTR falls from 0.6202 (Early Meccan) to 0.3005 (Medinan) across the four Cairo 1924 revelation periods, tracking word-unit count almost exactly; length-robust MATTR is nearly flat instead (0.8707-0.8913), and MTLD shows a smaller, less regular decline (673.77 down to 395.98, Medinan the outlier).
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-numbers.mjs using scripts/lib/lexical-diversity.mjs, written to data/numbers.json. Full table on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: 18,408 recurring sequences
caseStudies.claim: 18,408 distinct 3-5-word sequences recur somewhere else in the Qur'an: 6,403 by root sequence and 12,005 by surface form.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Generated by scripts/build-formulas.mjs, written to data/formulas-root.json and data/formulas-surface.json. Browse every one on Formulas.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: surah 64's formulaic density beats a length-matched null
caseStudies.claim: 55.6% of surah 64's words (root stream) belong to a phrase recurring elsewhere in the Qur'an, the highest of any surah, and higher than 10,000 length-matched resamples of the whole corpus predict (p=0.0001, survives Benjamini-Hochberg at q<0.05).
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-formulaic-density.mjs, written to data/formulaic-density.json. Panel on the surah 64 dossier; corpus-wide ranking on Formulas.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: j-h-m dispersion: range alone understates its concentration
caseStudies.claim: j-h-m (Hellfire) occurs in 18 of 114 surahs -- moderate by plain range -- but its normalized Deviation of Proportions is 0.7989, near the top of the ranking-eligible range, because those 18 surahs are disproportionately short.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-dispersion.mjs, written to data/dispersion/juHm.json. Method note in data/dispersion/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view; ranking table on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: extended association measures
caseStudies.claim: For gh-f-r and r-h-m (91 shared verses; gh-f-r in 202 verses, r-h-m in 313), the extended table gives logDice 12.50, t-score 8.48, log odds ratio 3.07 (95% interval 2.76 to 3.37), and deltaP 0.414 (r-h-m given gh-f-r) against 0.272 (gh-f-r given r-h-m). The measures rank pairs differently by design.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-exports.mjs with scripts/lib/association-measures.mjs from the published verse counts, written to data/exports/association-extended.json. logDice follows Rychlý (2008). Checked against a hand-computed 2x2 table in scripts/association-measures.test.mjs. Download on Export.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: distance between surahs, against a permutation null
caseStudies.claim: Al-Baqarah (2) and Al-Imran (3) have a Jensen-Shannon root distance of 0.384 against a permutation-null mean of 0.345 (excess 0.039, permutation p 0.0005, BH q 0.0009). Al-Baqarah and At-Tawbah (9) are 0.482 against 0.375 (excess 0.107). Both are well above chance for their lengths, and the second more so; neither number says what the surahs differ in.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-surah-distance.mjs from the Leeds v0.4 rooted tokens, written to data/surah-distance/surah-distance.json and published as the surah-distance table on Export. The distance is the square root of the Jensen-Shannon divergence (Lin 1991; a metric, Endres & Schindelin 2003). Checked against hand-computed cases in scripts/surah-distance.test.mjs. The null reassigns verses between the two surahs at random with sizes fixed (2,000 draws, fixed seed).

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: templates with one open slot
caseStudies.claim: The template وما _ من (wa-ma, any word, min) occurs 92 times where word order alone predicts about 25 (q 4.5e-22), and إن _ إلا (in, any word, illa) 90 times against about 11 (q 4.5e-46). In all, 1,003 of 1,669 candidate templates pass at q <= 0.05 and cover 26.6% of the corpus's words, while the same procedure on 100 verse-shuffled copies finds 0.06 on average. This records recurrence, not composition.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-formulaic-templates.mjs from the Leeds v0.4 surface forms, written to data/formulaic-templates.json and shown on Formulas. The expectation under a within-verse shuffle is exact and was checked against all permutations of small verses in scripts/templates.test.mjs. Whether a recurring template is a formula in the oral-formulaic sense is a scholarly question (Bannister 2014) this site does not decide.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: period keyness against a surah-level null
caseStudies.claim: Of 6,568 root-period tests, 132 pass Benjamini-Hochberg at q <= 0.05 against random assignment of whole surahs to the four periods. Of the 15 roots the Numbers page lists as most key for each period by G2 alone, 9 (Early Meccan), 5 (Middle Meccan), 5 (Late Meccan) and 14 (Medinan) pass; the rest are as strong as one long surah's own vocabulary makes them. One of 40 relabeled chronologies passes anything.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-period-keyness.mjs from the Leeds v0.4 morphology and data/chronology.json, written to data/keyness/period-keyness.json and published as the keyness-period table on Export. G2 follows Dunning (1993); q is Benjamini-Hochberg (1995). Checked against a hand-computed value and an exact enumeration of a toy corpus in scripts/keyness.test.mjs. The lists are marked on Numbers; the calibration is on Validation.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: does a root pair's association change across periods?
caseStudies.claim: For k-dh-b (lie) and r-b-b (lord), the verse-level log odds ratio is 2.04 (95% interval 1.55 to 2.54) in the Medinan period and -0.46 (-1.11 to 0.19) in the Late Meccan; Cochran's Q is 53.0 and the Benjamini-Hochberg q 9.4e-8. Only 14 of 5,203 pairs differ across the four periods at q <= 0.05, but the test is conservative (about 1% of pairs reach raw p <= 0.05 on randomly labeled verses), so that count is a lower bound, not a statement that the rest are stable.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Built by scripts/build-exports.mjs through scripts/lib/association-by-period.mjs and published as the association-by-period table on Export. The log odds ratio is Haldane-Anscombe with a Wald interval; Q follows Cochran (1954). A sample of pairs is recounted from the token files in scripts/association-by-period.test.mjs.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: templates with two and three open slots
caseStudies.claim: With two open slots, 715 of 1,558 candidate templates pass at q <= 0.05 (shuffled copies of the text: 0.03 on average, at most 2); with three, 534 of 1,328 (0.13 on average, at most 2, and 12 of 100 copies have any, above the nominal 5%). The widths overlap, so the counts do not add. This records where a pattern recurs, not why.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-formulaic-templates.mjs with scripts/lib/templates.mjs, written to data/formulaic-templates.json and shown on Formulas. The expectation under a within-verse shuffle is exact for each gap and was checked against all permutations of small verses in scripts/templates.test.mjs.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: what the methods report in noise
caseStudies.claim: On texts whose verses are shuffled across the whole Qur'an and cut into pseudo-surahs of the real surahs' sizes, the surah-distance pipeline gives raw p <= 0.05 for 4.93% of pairs (nominal 5%), no pair passing Benjamini-Hochberg, and a mean excess of -0.0004; on the real text 5,248 of 6,441 pairs pass. The period-association test is conservative (about 1% of pairs at raw p <= 0.05), and period keyness passes something in 1 of 40 relabeled chronologies.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-calibration.mjs, written to data/calibration/report.json and shown on Validation. The template and keyness rows are read back from the files whose scripts already ran those null copies.
